labels.text: No agents found. Create one with: /agents create <name>

S61.01.needs: none (an agent must exist; create one first with S61.02 steps)
S61.01.note: The roster is the list of markdown agent files in .agiworkforce/agents/ (project) and ~/.agiworkforce/agents/ (global). The app's own text says "Agents" and "[project]"/"[global]" scope tags; check the exact scope text in the overlay.
steps: Start agi and sign in.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Look for the overlay titled Agents with a list of agent names, each showing its color, scope ([project] or [global]) and description.
Compare with Expected: each persistent agent is listed by name. If you have no agents, the overlay shows "No agents found. Create one with: /agents create <name>".
S61.01.where: Type /agents in the chat (the TUI opens an overlay titled "Agents"). In plain text mode, /agents prints "Agents (N)" with a table.

S61.02.needs: a folder agi can write to
S61.02.note: Creating from a plain-words description needs a model reply; the blank-template path needs no model.
steps: Type /agents create reviewer and press Enter.
Read the reply: it should say Created project agent `reviewer` at a path ending in .agiworkforce/agents/reviewer.md.
Type /agents and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the new agent appears in the roster by name.
S61.02.where: Type /agents create <name> in the chat (add --global to save it for every project). A description in words instead of a name also works and is drafted by the model.

S61.03.needs: an existing agent named reviewer (create one first)
S61.03.note: Expected says name and avatar. The code has a user-set name and a color, but no avatar; apps/cli was searched for avatar and only a routing regex matched. The avatar part of the item cannot be tested.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer color blue and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and read the color line.
Type /agents and press Enter, then look at the reviewer name in the overlay.
Compare with Expected: the name shows in the chosen color. No avatar exists to check.
S61.03.where: Type /agents set <name> color <color> (colors: red, blue, green, yellow, purple, orange, pink, cyan). There is no avatar or picture setting anywhere in the CLI code.

steps: Type /agents set reviewer description "Reviews pull requests for risky changes" and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the description line shows the text you wrote.
S61.04.where: Type /agents set <name> description <text>, then read it back with /agents show <name>.

S61.05.note: The prompt field replaces the markdown body, which becomes the system prompt. The effect on behaviour is model-driven and only visible in replies.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer prompt "Check every change for missing tests" and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and press Enter.
Look for the prompt body in the output.
Compare with Expected: the agent's own instructions are the text shown. To see the effect, run the agent with /agents reviewer and ask it for a review.
S61.05.where: Type /agents set <name> prompt <text> to replace the agent's instructions, then read them with /agents show <name>.

S61.08.note: No account-level sharing of tools or connectors per agent was found. Agents have their own tools and disallowedTools lists and per-agent maxTurns and maxBudgetUsd (src/agents.rs). A separate /connectors command exists (apps/cli/src/claude_parity.rs) but it is session-level, not per agent. Searched apps/cli for connector and agents.rs for account-level sharing.

S61.09.note: Skills are preloaded per agent (skills field), not shared at account level in the code; the agent shows what it preloads.
steps: Type /skills and press Enter and note the installed skill names.
Type /agents set reviewer skills <name> (a comma-separated list of installed skills) and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and read the skills line.
Compare with Expected: the agent shows the skills it can use, and they match the installed skills from /skills.
S61.09.where: Type /agents show <name> to see the skills line for an agent; type /skills to list the installed skills.

S61.13.note: Activation applies the agent's model, budget and instructions to the current session. Whether the reply sounds like the agent is model-driven.
steps: Type /agents and press Enter.
Choose an agent and press Enter.
Look for the reply Agent `<name>` activated (with the model name if the agent sets one).
Send a message and compare with Expected: the reply follows that agent's instructions and role.
S61.13.where: Type /agents in the chat, move to an agent with the arrow keys, and press Enter. Or type /agents <name> directly.

S61.14.note: Without --team the app says "Agent teams are off in this session"; teammates are created by the lead agent, so the exact team depends on the model.
steps: Start agi --team in a terminal.
Ask the lead in plain words to bring in two teammates for a task.
Type /team and press Enter to see the team messages and status.
Compare with Expected: several agents post messages in one shared conversation, each message shown with its sender.
S61.14.where: Start with agi --team (or set AGI_TEAM=1), ask the lead to bring in teammates, then type /team to see the team.

S61.15.note: The coordinator behaviour is set by the lead's brief in the code and decided by the model, so it is not a menu. Teammates are named by the lead.
steps: Start agi --team in a terminal.
Ask the lead for a task that needs two specialists, for example a review and a summary.
Watch the team lines and the lead's final reply.
Compare with Expected: the lead hands parts of the work to the other agents and then reports to you.
S61.15.where: Start agi --team, then ask the lead (named lead in the code) for a task that needs several specialists. The lead routes the work and reports back.

S61.16.note: Delegation is a model tool call (agent tool, action run) in apps/cli/src/agent/chat.rs. There is no button; whether the model chooses to delegate is model-driven.
steps: Type /agents and press Enter and note an agent name.
Ask the main agent in plain words to have that agent do one part of a task.
Watch the tool line in the transcript that names the agent.
Compare with Expected: the specialist's result appears and the main agent uses it in its answer.
S61.16.where: Type /agents to see the installed agents, then ask the main agent in plain words to hand part of a task to one of them by name. The main agent calls its agent tool.

S61.17.note: Messages go through the send_message tool (apps/cli/src/agent/tools.rs). Whether an agent sends one is model-driven.
steps: Start agi --team and ask the lead to have two teammates work together on a task.
Type /team and press Enter.
Look for lines of the form sender to receiver with the message text.
Compare with Expected: the receiving agent acts on the message and the exchange is visible to you.
S61.17.where: Start agi --team, have the lead or a teammate send a message to another teammate, then type /team to read the message history.

S61.18.note: The escalation text is produced by the teammate's send_message to the user; whether it happens is model-driven.
steps: Start agi --team and ask the lead to have a teammate check with you before a decision.
Watch for a line saying the teammate asks you, followed by a line Answer with /team <name> <your answer>.
Type /team <name> followed by your answer and press Enter.
Compare with Expected: the teammate receives your answer and continues the work.
S61.18.where: Start agi --team, ask a teammate to make a decision that needs you, then answer with /team <name> <your answer>.

S61.20.needs: an existing agent named reviewer; a model account to run it
S61.20.note: Enforcement is in code (agent cap_spend and session max_turns in apps/cli/src/agents.rs) but is visible only during a run.
steps: Type /agents set reviewer maxBudgetUsd 0.50 and press Enter.
Type /agents set reviewer maxTurns 5 and press Enter.
Type /agents show reviewer and look for the spend cap per run line and the max_turns line.
Compare with Expected: the limits show for the agent. To check enforcement, run the agent with /agents reviewer on a task that would go over the limit and see that it stops.
S61.20.where: Type /agents set <name> maxBudgetUsd <dollars> and /agents set <name> maxTurns <number>, then read them with /agents show <name>.

S61.22.needs: at least one completed agent run
steps: Run an agent first with /agents <name> and send one request.
Type /agents history and press Enter.
Look for the runs with outcome, files and spend.
Compare with Expected: each agent's past runs are listed. If nothing ran yet, the text No recorded agent runs yet. appears.
S61.22.where: Type /agents history to see all agents' runs, or /agents history <name> for one agent.
